notes.summary: Compact boundaryless balanced rational embedding-chart spaces have endpoint regularity in both coefficient categories; locally literal PA obstacles have exact rational constant endpoints. Broader abstract compact categories are excluded.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves rational-carrier scalar extension, the continuous PA/PCC test, positive balanced star spanning by covolume-calibrated divergence, locally bounded rational completion, strong maximum principle, componentwise envelope minima, decreasing rational constants and local rational-minimum attainment without a global bounded-cell decomposition. Separately proves finite globally embedded positive-dimensional balanced supports cannot be compact. The atlas assumptions are binding; this does not classify compact boundary/quasi-embedded spaces without that atlas.
notes.text:
This unverified author draft proves a compact-sector theorem, not the entire P05.1 classification. The category is compact Hausdorff, pure-dimensional, boundaryless rational polyhedral spaces with homeomorphic embedding charts onto relatively open subsets of finite positive balanced rational supports. Overlaps are rational integral-affine lattice isomorphisms preserving PCC and balancing data. No global embedding or bounded-cell decomposition is assumed. Compactifications with an unbalanced boundary and merely cellwise quasi-embedded abstract spaces are not silently included.

Literal PA_Z has integral slopes on saturated tangent lattices and rational constants. PA_R is its finite real linear extension on rational carrying geometry. On a fixed finite rational carrier the matching conditions on all affine pieces are rational linear equations. A rational basis of this coefficient space, multiplied by suitable positive integers, consists of literal functions. Hence any real-coefficient affine data satisfying those matching conditions is in the scalar extension. Rational points are dense in every face of a rational polyhedron: impose its active rational equalities, row-reduce over Q, and approximate kernel coordinates while preserving strict inactive inequalities.

The PC convention is the printed rational-endpoint PCC test, with real nonnegative weights, center in a common incident face. It allows discontinuous downward modifications at irrational points. For example, zero on rational points and minus one elsewhere satisfies every printed PCC inequality. We assert endpoint regularity directly, not density in this discontinuous printed class. Continuous PA divisor positivity is equivalent to PCC. One-cycle positivity gives convexity along cell segments; at a rational center, rays toward rational endpoints with weights alpha_i times their primitive lengths form a balanced one-cycle, yielding nonnegative weighted directional derivative, bounded above by the endpoint secants. For real endpoints/centers use perspective variables s_i=alpha_i x_i: sum alpha_i=1, sum s_i in the center face, and A_i s_i>=alpha_i b_i are rational polyhedral constraints. Rational tuples are dense in their minimal face, and continuity passes the inequality. Conversely, for any effective k-cycle at a generic rational point of a (k-1)-face, its primitive normals satisfy b=sum w_sigma n_sigma in the tangent space. For rational weights choose one positive w_0 and replace n_0 by n_0-b/w_0. Small rational endpoints along these corrected directions give Jensen and therefore nonnegative tangent-corrected divisor. Approximate real balanced weights within their rational coefficient cone to conclude. An ambient affine lower support gives the same positivity directly. This repairs the continuous PA test without inserting an irrational center into a rational refinement.

Here is the balanced spanning argument. If c_sigma and c_tau are saturated Euclidean tangent covolumes, the projected primitive normal length is c_sigma/c_tau. Euclidean density mu_sigma=w_sigma c_sigma therefore has facet flux c_tau w_sigma n_sigma; balancing cancels it. If a star lay in a proper halfspace of its span, take a linear form ell nonnegative there and positive somewhere. Apply divergence to its constant tangent-projected vector on top cones truncated by the unit ball. Internal facets cancel and divergence is zero, so the outer angular integral of ell is zero. Positive weights and a positive angular patch contradict this. Finitely generated cones are closed: remove dependent active columns, use one of finitely many independent inverses to bound coefficients on bounded sets, and pass to a subsequence. Nearest-point separation would supply the forbidden halfspace if the cone were not its full span. Thus rational star generators v_i, including both signs of tangential generators, conically span the entire span. Express each -v_i nonnegatively in the generators using rational independent-column elimination and sum these relations. This gives sum lambda_i v_i=0 with every lambda_i positive rational. Dimension zero is immediate.

We reconstruct the locally bounded completion needed for actual envelopes. On a compact portion of relint(tau), for rational z choose uniform small rational epsilon and anchors z_i=z+epsilon v_i in their incident cells. A nearby rational y has y-z=sum a_i v_i, a_i>=0, sum a_i<=A||y-z||, using generators of its incident cone; independent-column elimination makes A uniform. If |q|<=B locally, the forward PCC gives q(y)-q(z)<=2B sum a_i/epsilon. Put t=max a_i/lambda_i and b_i=(t lambda_i-a_i)/epsilon. Then z=(y+sum b_i z_i)/(1+sum b_i), a legal reverse PCC at tau, and q(y)-q(z)>=-2B sum b_i. Both sums are O(||y-z||). Within each face rational values extend continuously. For a sequence y tending to an arbitrary p in relint(tau), choose rational z in tau with ||z-p||<=||y-p||. The uniform comparison identifies every incident-face limit with the face extension. Induction over the finite faces gives a single continuous completion F. Shrinking rational simplices in the minimal face give q(p)<=F(p). Perspective rational approximation as above gives all real-endpoint PCC inequalities. Dense rational overlap values and rational transitions make the local completions glue. Only local bounds are used.

For a continuous real-endpoint PC function attaining a maximum at p, the same star relation writes p as a PCC of every sufficiently nearby y and small star anchors, with a strictly positive weight on y. All endpoint values are at most the maximum. Equality at p forces equality at y. Thus the maximum set is open and closed. Compact connected components are constant. Polyhedral charts are locally connected, so components are open; compactness makes their number finite and each closed and compact.

Let gamma be a continuous PC reference and u continuous on the compact space. The unrestricted envelope E is the supremum of all finite printed PC competitors differing boundedly from gamma and lying below gamma+u. The competitor gamma-||u|| bounds E below, while the obstacle bounds it above. Suprema preserve PCC, so the bounded completion construction gives continuous F>=E. Its rational values are below the continuous obstacle, hence it is below that obstacle everywhere; it still differs boundedly from gamma and is a competitor. Therefore F<=E and E=F. The maximum principle makes gamma and E componentwise constant. On each component D, E equals min_D(gamma+u), because that componentwise constant is itself a competitor and no larger constant is below the obstacle.

These finitely many constants are real PA and admit literal decreasing uniform approximation by 2^(-n) ceil(2^n c_D), with error below 2^(-n). For a locally literal PA obstacle, a minimizer p lies in the relative interior of some chart carrying cell tau. Its affine derivative vanishes in every tangent direction, so its value is constant on tau. A rational point there has the same rational affine value. Thus the minimum is rational and the endpoint itself is literal PA, without a global bounded-cell decomposition.

Finally, a nonempty finite globally embedded positive balanced support of dimension d>=1 cannot be compact. With the Euclidean densities above, the tangent-projected field Y(x)=x has divergence d on every bounded top cell. All facet fluxes cancel and there is no external boundary, contradicting a positive sum of weighted cell volumes. This does not exclude compact spaces assembled from charts.

Exactly A224/B225/R230/S262/S272 and all their clarifications are granted inputs; report labels and working papers are data. The fresh compact proof reconstructs its spanning, bounded completion, maximum and rational-minimum steps. Ordinary real completeness, finite-dimensional compactness, Gaussian elimination, elementary calculus and polytope divergence are disclosed foundations. Source versions, whole immediate units read and application restrictions are recorded in source-application-ledger.md; no delegated unavailable source theorem is used for this proof. notes.summary: Global affine real-PA approximation preserves rational carrying geometry and exact actual-reference recession, and interpolates every prescribed finite rational set; it gives decreasing uniform approximation.
notes.detailedSummary: For a complete rational affine plane and an actual finite rational-carrier positive real-PA convex reference, proves finite convex continuity/duality and polyhedral representation, compact-dual boundary continuity, finite rational sample majorants with a global error bound, rational projected graph faces and exact recession. Heights/slopes may be irrational. Prescribed interpolation belongs to the unshifted majorants; rational common shifts give the decreasing sequence. No singular-union extension is inferred.
notes.text:
Theorem: on a complete rational affine d-plane V with actual finite rational-carrier convex gamma in PA_R positive at infinity, every continuous convex f with ||f-gamma|| finite has, for every eta>0 and finite rational S, a finite rational-carrier convex PA_R majorant F satisfying f<=F<=f+eta globally, F(s)=f(s) for s in S, and F^infinity=gamma^infinity. No reference heights or slopes are assumed rational. This is a global theorem and does not extend by itself to a nonconvex singular support. The coefficient/category and divisor facts used are proved in n1.

We supply the finite convex foundations. A cone {Ax>=0} splits off ker A. On its complement ell=sum_j(Ax)_j is strictly positive on the cone except zero; its ell=1 section is bounded, since an unbounded sequence normalized to unit length would give ell=0 there. A bounded polyhedron is the convex hull of finitely many vertices: from a nonvertex move in both directions annihilating all active equalities until a new independent inequality becomes active; express the point as their convex combination and induct on active rank. There are only finitely many independent active systems. This generates the cone; add both signs of lineality generators. Homogenizing {Ax>=b} with t>=0, Ax-tb>=0 gives vertices from generators t>0 and recession rays from t=0. Rational systems give rational choices. Conversely, expressing a point as a convex combination of point generators plus a nonnegative combination of ray generators and eliminating variables by pairing lower and upper bounds (Fourier–Motzkin) gives finitely many weak inequalities. The generated set is a closed polyhedron. Equality in a supporting functional retains exactly its minimal point generators and zero ray generators.

Finite convex functions on the whole plane are continuous. Enclose a ball of radius 2r in a cube and let B be the maximum at its vertices. Convexity bounds values above by B; reflection in its center x bounds them below on the radius-r ball by 2f(x)-B. Extend each short secant to length r to bound its slope by 2(B-f(x))/r on the radius-r/2 ball, in both directions. For an affine support at x project (x,f(x)-t) to the closed epigraph, normalize the separating projection normals and let t decrease to zero. Contact points approach (x,f(x)). The limiting vertical normal is nonpositive and cannot be zero, since a nonzero horizontal functional cannot be bounded on the full spatial projection. Division gives an affine support. Taking supports proves f=f**.

Write gamma=max_j(a_j.x+b_j), h=gamma^infinity=max_j a_j.x, Delta=conv{a_j}. Each full-dimensional affine piece of a convex PA function is a global support, proving this expression. Gamma-h is bounded and h(v)>0 for v!=0, so 0 is interior to Delta. Recession cones of the finite rational carrier cover V: some cell meets unboundedly many points of any spatial ray, and its inequalities put that direction in its recession cone. Subdivide them into pointed rational cones and choose rational ray generators r_k. As h is linear on each recession cone, epi h is cone{(r_k,h(r_k)),(0,1)}. Heights may be irrational; spatial rays remain rational.

The Legendre transform f*(p)=sup_x(p.x-f(x)) has domain exactly Delta and is uniformly bounded there, since f-h is bounded. Outside Delta a separating direction v gives p.v>h(v) and an infinite supremum along that ray. It is convex and lower semicontinuous. A finite lower-semicontinuous convex function g on a compact polytope is continuous even at the boundary: bound it above by B=max g at the vertices; at p choose r smaller than every inactive inequality's slack divided by normal norm. For nearby y in the polytope, z=p+r(y-p)/||y-p|| stays in it. Convexity gives g(y)<=g(p)+(||y-p||/r)(B-g(p)), while lower semicontinuity gives the reverse limiting bound. Thus f* is continuous on Delta.

Continuity of f lets its transform be computed using only rational x. For each p choose a rational near optimizer with error less than eta/2. Continuity of f* makes its error less than eta on a neighborhood of p. A finite subcover, with S added, gives a finite rational set A and g_A(p)=max_{x in A}(p.x-f(x)) with f*(p)-eta<=g_A(p)<=f*(p) for all p in Delta.

Set E_A=conv{(x,f(x)):x in A}+epi h. It is a closed polyhedron, projects onto all V, and is upward closed. Dual support yields f(x+v)<=f(x)+h(v), so convexity puts E_A inside epi f. Its vertical fibers have finite lower endpoints and define a finite convex PA function F_A. Direct maximization over the point and ray generators gives F_A*=g_A on Delta and infinity outside Delta. Double duality gives f<=F_A<=f+eta on the entire unbounded plane. Each prescribed lifted point belongs to E_A, so F_A(s)=f(s).

Each graph face of E_A is generated by a subset of its lifted points and zero-support rays, never the vertical ray. Its projection is the convex hull of rational spatial points plus a cone of rational spatial rays. The polyhedral facts just proved make it rational. Projection is injective on the graph, so common graph faces project to common faces. These finitely many projections provide an actual rational carrying complex. The rational coefficient-space argument of n1 puts the real function in PA_R; ordinary convex supports give genuine PA positivity. Thus no irrational maximum wall is treated as rational geometry. Exact recession follows from rec(E_A)=epi h: the convex hull of lifted points is bounded; divide a ray sequence by its length and use closedness of epi h for the reverse inclusion. Also the global error gives bounded difference from the actual gamma.

Choose eta_n=2^(-n) and majorants F_n. Then G_n=F_n+4*2^(-n) has 0<=G_n-f<=5*2^(-n), while G_n-G_(n+1)>=4*2^(-n)-5*2^(-n-1)>0. Rational constant shifts preserve carrier and exact recession. This gives decreasing global uniform approximation. The unshifted majorants interpolate S exactly; the shifted sequence does not retain exact interpolation, but uses a common rational shift.

The result reconstructs the needed affine route from unreviewed 282/283/284 data; none of their conclusions is imported as a grant. It proves no all-conical or arbitrary singular-union statement. notes.summary: Independent complete affine branches meeting at a rational point have all-continuous real regularity for every actual real reference; synchronized interpolation handles arbitrary continuous branch data.
notes.detailedSummary: Characterizes continuous PC by branchwise ordinary convexity when tangent spaces form a direct sum. Reconstructs actual unrestricted envelope continuity from bounded local completion. Uses n2 to interpolate the shared origin and glue genuine rational-carrier PA approximants with all-face positivity, exact recession and common decreasing shifts. Gives synchronized capped convex roofs and exact finite-PA endpoints for finite PA obstacles. Positive-dimensional intersections and dependent branches are not covered.
notes.text:
An independent affine bouquet is a finite union X=union_i(a+V_i) of complete rational d-planes with rational a, constant positive weights, saturated tangent lattices, and a direct sum of the V_i. In this geometric sector every actual positive-at-infinity finite rational-carrier real-PA reference has endpoint regularity for every bounded continuous obstacle. This includes arbitrary non-PA branch data and mixed coordinate dependence inside a branch. It does not include dependent planes or positive-dimensional branch overlaps. The compact/completion facts of n1 and interpolation theorem of n2 are used.

First, continuous PC is exactly ordinary convexity on each branch with a shared value at a. Necessity: on a rational segment in one branch use a finite rational subdivision. In each cell the PCC test gives convexity. At crossings, the two-sided PCC centered in the common face orders the left and right secant slopes; concatenation gives convexity of the whole segment, including a crossing at a. Continuity extends to real segments. Conversely, at any center away from a all incident cells belong to one plane, and ordinary convexity proves Jensen. At a, group PCC endpoints by branch. Independence forces the weighted spatial sum in each branch separately to be zero. For each nonempty group, convexity gives its weighted values at least its total weight times f(a); summing proves the entire PCC. These arguments cover every face, rather than only origin circuits.

The actual unrestricted envelope E for continuous gamma and u in C_b is between gamma-||u|| and gamma+u. It is finite PCC by taking the supremum. On every compact chart portion it is bounded, so n1's local star comparison gives a continuous completion F>=E. Rational comparisons with the continuous upper and lower bounds show F still satisfies them everywhere and differs boundedly from gamma. It is an eligible competitor, so F<=E and E=F. Hence E is continuous PC before regularization, without restricting the defining competitors to continuous ones. Translating competitors also proves ||P_gamma(u)-P_gamma(v)||<=||u-v||. No global C_b density of local obstacle approximations is asserted.

For any such continuous PC f, apply n2 on every plane with the same error 2^(-n) and prescribed rational set {a}. The majorants F_i,n have value f(a) at a, global error at most 2^(-n), and the exact recession of the actual gamma_i. Glue them. Refining each rational carrier by rational orthants makes a a common vertex, without any equality wall determined by irrational heights. The glued carrier is finite and rational, and n1's coefficient-space argument gives PA_R. The branch characterization gives every PCC inequality. Genuine divisor positivity can also be checked directly: at a choose an affine support on every branch with common constant f(a); direct-sum independence extends their linear parts simultaneously to one ambient affine support. At a nonorigin point a small neighborhood meets only its one plane and has the ordinary convex support. The tangent-corrected divisor test from n1 applies with saturated normals and all effective cycles. Add the same rational constant 4*2^(-n) on every branch. Values remain synchronized, and n2's estimate gives a decreasing global uniform sequence in the actual same-reference class. This puts every actual envelope in the genuine PA_R regularizable domain before any raw operator completion is invoked.

There is also an explicit synchronized convex-roof formula. For b_i=gamma_i+u_i let H_i be its greatest ordinary convex minorant and c=min_i H_i(a). Define Q_i as its greatest convex minorant with Q_i(a)<=c. Gamma_i-||u|| bounds H_i below; it is finite convex and continuous. H_i-(H_i(a)-c) is an admissible capped minorant, so Q_i(a)=c and Q_i has the same growth. The Q_i glue as PC. The actual continuous envelope has branch restrictions bounded by H_i and a common value at most c, hence is bounded by Q_i. The glued Q_i is itself a competitor, proving equality.

For finite rational-carrier PA_R b_i, take a pointed carrying refinement. Each epigraph piece is generated by lifted rational spatial vertices, lifted rational spatial recession rays with real heights, and a vertical ray. Bounded difference from gamma_i gives the exact gamma_i recession heights. Its closed convex hull is the convex hull of all lifted vertices plus epi gamma_i^infinity; adding (a,c) produces the capped roof. The shifted H_i bounds its lower boundary below. Every graph face projects to a rational polyhedron generated by subsets of rational positions and rays, as in n2. Thus this PA obstacle envelope itself is finite rational-carrier PA_R even when heights are irrational.

This is a geometric regularity theorem, not a classification by the defining envelope condition. A product of a cross with a line has positive-dimensional common traces and is not covered. notes.summary: Every finite noncompact support with a literal positive reference has a bounded literal obstacle with a fractional-slope envelope and a positive uniform literal-approximation error floor.
notes.detailedSummary: Reconstructs the compact-gap/vertex-cone obstacle, proves its actual unrestricted envelope by vertex and recession PCC, and proves the integer-slope convex approximation floor L dist(q0,Z)/4. Balancing is unnecessary. Applies n1 noncompactness to all positive-dimensional finite globally embedded balanced literal pairs, without eliminating compact chart spaces. No measure is assigned to the nonregularizable literal endpoint.
notes.text:
We reconstruct the literal negative sector: every finite globally embedded noncompact rational polyhedral support with a literal PA_Z polyhedrally convex reference gamma positive at infinity has a bounded literal obstacle whose actual unrestricted envelope is not uniformly regularizable by literal PC PA functions. Balancing is unnecessary. On positive-dimensional finite globally embedded positive balanced supports, n1 proves noncompactness, so every admitted literal reference fails regularity. This does not eliminate compact chart spaces, which n1 treats positively.

Choose a noncompact connected component, rational p there and rational C>gamma(p). Put phi=max(gamma,C) and D=phi-gamma. Rational coefficients make every inserted wall rational and phi remains PC by the max Jensen inequality and n1's continuous PA test. D is literal, nonnegative, positive at p, and compactly supported. Indeed on each pointed carrying cell gamma has positive recession slope on its unit recession section; its vertex part is bounded. Finitely many cells give gamma(x)>=kappa||x||-A outside a bounded set. Take a finite pointed rational common refinement carrying gamma and D. On an unbounded cell, bounded affine D has zero recession slopes; translating along any nonzero recession direction eventually leaves its compact support. Thus D is identically zero there.

Finite polyhedral connected components are path connected. A path from p to a far zero of D meets a bounded positive-dimensional carrying cell with nonzero affine slope k for D. Choose a primitive lattice direction w there with k(w)!=0 and a rational segment a+[0,L]w in its relative interior. For integer N>|k(w)| let f=gamma+D/N=(1-1/N)gamma+(1/N)phi. It is continuous PC with the same growth and has nonintegral slope q_0=m+k(w)/N on that segment, where m is integral.

For each carrying vertex v, an ambient integral coordinate norm rho(x)=max_j|ell_j(x)| and sufficiently large common integer M give D(v)/N+M rho(x-v)>=D(x)/N on X. Near v this follows from its finitely many incident affine slopes; outside a neighborhood the bounded numerator divided by rho(x-v) is bounded. Define u=min{D, min_v(D(v)/N+M rho(x-v))}. Every slope is integral, every constant rational, and all min/max walls rational. It is bounded, D/N<=u<=D, has u(v)=D(v)/N, and vanishes on unbounded carrying cells. Therefore f is a competitor below gamma+u.

For any printed PC competitor q below this obstacle, a point of a bounded cell is a convex combination of rational vertices; their obstacle values are f and f is affine, so q<=f there. On an unbounded pointed cell write y=sum alpha_j v_j+sum beta_k r_k, with alpha,beta nonnegative and sum alpha=1. Pick v_0 with alpha_0>0 and large rational T satisfying sum beta_k/T<=alpha_0. Transfer those weights from v_0 to rational endpoints v_0+T r_k. They have weighted average y. On this entire cell D=u=0, so its obstacle equals affine f=gamma. PCC gives q(y)<=f(y), even for real y and real weights, since endpoints are rational. Thus the actual unrestricted envelope is exactly f on every cell.

Any literal PC PA approximant psi has nondecreasing integer slopes along the primitive segment. Let k' be its right slope at the midpoint. If k'<=floor(q_0), use the left half-segment; if k'>=ceil(q_0), use the right half-segment. In either case the difference of the endpoint errors has absolute size at least (L/2) dist(q_0,Z). Each error is bounded by ||psi-f||, so ||psi-f||>=(L/4) dist(q_0,Z)>0. Literal uniform or decreasing-uniform approximation is impossible. No literal Monge–Ampere measure is assigned to this endpoint.

The simplest exact example is gamma=|x|, u=min(1/2,(1-|x|)_+), envelope f=max(|x|,(|x|+1)/2). Its fractional segment slope is 1/2 on [0,1] and the proved uniform error floor is 1/8. Grid evaluation is only supporting evidence; the vertex/recession proof establishes the envelope and the slope argument establishes the floor.

notes.text:
The complete original P05.1 remains unresolved and candidate=false. The fresh deliverable proves compact chart regularity in both coefficient categories (n1), global same-actual-reference affine approximation with rational interpolation (n2), all-continuous real regularity on independent affine bouquets (n3), and the finite noncompact literal obstruction (n4). Execution evidence in n5 has no acceptance force. No defining density/envelope statement is offered as the missing geometric classification.

The exact unresolved real sectors are general higher-dimensional singular balanced supports and their all-face coefficient-cone constrained approximation over arbitrary rational refinements; dependent affine branches; positive-dimensional common traces; and arbitrary nonseparable obstacles on products of singular graphs/spaces. Separate factor regularity, separable envelope formulas, finite origin circuits or a fixed-fan polynomial contact test do not solve those cases. The bouquet theorem does allow arbitrary continuous nonseparable coordinate data inside a complete branch, but finite interpolation at one point does not synchronize a non-PA trace on a positive-dimensional intersection.

The compact result is complete only under n1's stated boundaryless positive balanced rational embedding atlas with compatible rational integral-affine transitions. If the original abstract category permits only cellwise quasi-embeddings, incompatible rational structures or boundary compactifications without that atlas, their intrinsic completion/maximum proof or reduction remains open here. Finite globally embedded noncompactness cannot erase them. No unrestricted all-conical assertion is used, and a quadratic finite-distance PCC margin is not promoted to a first-order slope floor.

The supplied whole S262 all-continuous finite embedded graph theorem is retained as a granted sector, with its domain and qualifications unchanged. The supplied S272 mixed completion applies only after actual global real-PA regularization. On the finite bouquets n3 first constructs that domain membership; only then may its exact primitive saturated recursion be completed for the actual REAL reference. Its rational positive component gamma_0 stays within the actual coefficient face in gamma=gamma'+epsilon gamma_0. On each fixed-C relative family the proper-height moment is bounded by (2d/epsilon) C deg(gamma)+J0, J0=int H0 MA(gamma). Ordinary weak/net continuity and all bounded-continuous tests are retained; weak/BL uniform continuity is only on each fixed-C slice, while global vague uniformity is separate. There is no inferred global weak/BL modulus or general continuous-PC domain membership. In positive dimension compact endpoints are locally constant, so their primitive divisor and positive-order iterates are zero directly; dimension-zero mass is not declared zero. No probability normalization by zero mass, analytic calibration or orthogonality classification is claimed.

Exactly the five caller grants and every clarification were read whole. Working 282/283/284 and the older independent-branch paper/review were read as data and the used mathematics independently reconstructed; their labels give no authority. Unused 276/277/278/281/285 and the historical native-final emitter/result were not mathematical dependencies. Whole immediate essential original BMPS/BBGS units, versions, domains, application restrictions and recursive foundations are disclosed in source-application-ledger.md. Ordinary foundations are real completeness, finite-dimensional compactness, Gaussian elimination, elementary calculus/integration and polytope divergence; the optional whole mixed theory is granted rather than newly reconstructed in all its recursive foundations. No unavailable fifth-source theorem or forthcoming sequel fills a gap.
